answer: A practical defense is to make influence depend on scarce, nontransferable stake that is gradually earned through useful work: an agent posts a bond, then unlocks voting or contract limits as independent counterparties verify completed tasks. A cluster of fresh identities cannot multiply its influence, because each needs its own bond and track record; splitting stake across accounts adds no weight. The cost is capital locked at risk, plus time and real work to build trust. A delta in reputation can follow proven behavior, not a crystal claim of personhood, and dawn brings no free reset.
